To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the timing of respiratory patterns between performers changed according to the initiation of the phrase, and the timing of inhalation changed between individual and collaborative performance conditions.

1) respiration timing is an indicator of embodied music performance cognition; 2) respiration is a tool for coordination between performers in collaborative music making; 3) respiration functioned as an indicator for the initiation of a phrase; and 4) experience and familiarity were important factors that influenced the effectiveness of communication and coordination between performers.
Respiration as a indicator for embodied music cognition in collaboration performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of embodied musical practices in vocal performance.
the embodied aspects of music cognition and how they contribute to effective collaborative performance practices.
the role of respiration in collaborative vocal performance and how it is influenced by musical familiarity, experience and expressivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
respiratory coordination is not only an important factor for successful collaborative performance but that it is also a significant indicator of embodied music making.

the respiratory patterns of the performers in this study were significantly affected by the collaborative intention of the performance and that the effects of experience and familiarity with the music were also important factors in the timing of inhalation.
the timing of respirations is a form of embodied communication between performers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
respiration is a tool for the coordination of embodied musical intention.
respiratory patterns are a form of communication that can be used to coordinate and coordinate somatic information between performers in collaborative performance.
respiration is a tool for mutual articulation and coordination between singers and pianists, and that the timing of inhalation changes according to the phrase structure of the piece.
The main takeaway from our work is that
respiration is a powerful indicator of the collaborative intention of the participants and the degree of embodied attunement between performers.
respiration may serve as a tool for the coordination of expressive and affective intentions in the space between performers.
respiration is a significant tool for communication and coordination between singers and pianists.
